steps.title: Venn overlap
steps.prompt: What belongs where two Venn hoops overlap?
steps.hint: The overlap is inside both hoops.
steps.explanation: The overlap satisfies both sorting rules.
steps.shortExplanation: The overlap satisfies both sorting rules.

steps.title: Colour pattern
steps.prompt: red, blue, red, blue... What comes next?
steps.hint: Say the colours aloud and find the part that repeats.
steps.explanation: The repeated part is red, blue.
steps.shortExplanation: The repeated part is red, blue.

steps.title: Tens and ones in 15
steps.prompt: 15 has how many tens and ones?
steps.hint: The first digit counts tens; the second counts ones.
steps.explanation: 15 is one whole ten and five ones.
steps.shortExplanation: 15 is one whole ten and five ones.

steps.title: Every day for a week
steps.prompt: Omar plays outside every day for one week. How many days is that?
steps.hint: Say the days from Sunday to Saturday and count them.
steps.explanation: One week has seven days, from Sunday to Saturday.
steps.shortExplanation: One week has seven days, from Sunday to Saturday.

steps.title: Balance rule
steps.prompt: On a balance, does the heavier side go up or down?
steps.hint: Look at the balance. Which pan is lower?
steps.explanation: More mass makes that side go down.
steps.shortExplanation: More mass makes that side go down.

steps.title: Partner of 8
steps.hint: Fill 8 spaces of a ten frame. How many are empty?

steps.title: Difference of 7 and 10
steps.prompt: What is the difference between 7 and 10?
steps.hint: Start on 7 and count the jumps to 10.
steps.explanation: Three forward jumps lead from seven to ten.
steps.shortExplanation: Three forward jumps lead from seven to ten.

steps.title: Half of 8
steps.explanation: Share eight equally into two groups of four.
steps.shortExplanation: Share eight equally into two groups of four.

steps.title: Equal halves
steps.prompt: Two halves of the same whole can have different sizes.
steps.hint: Can halves of the same whole be different sizes?
steps.explanation: Halves of the same whole are always equal.
steps.shortExplanation: Halves of the same whole are always equal.
